summary: Reproduced the delayed final-prefill abort race on the prepared main: an aborted prefill entered optimistic decode and committed token 101 before consuming the abort. Added guards at scheduler admission and prefill-result commit, preserving mixed-decode behavior and packed metadata cursor alignment.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before reproduction: 3 failed, 11 passed, 2 subtests passed; observed optimistic-decode admission, output_ids changing from [] to [101], and abort precedence loss.

Passing-after regression and independent boundaries: 20 passed and 2 subtests passed, covering pending-result admission, already-processed results, mixed decode membership, hidden/custom/logprob cursor behavior, sampling-mask precedence, and grammar advancement.
Additional deferred chunked-abort and grammar boundary coverage: 8 passed.
Patched source-checkout server performed real gfx950 prefill/decode; /generate, /v1/completions, two-request batch, and streaming completion all returned HTTP 200, with 8 stream events.
Touched Python modules compile and the patch has no whitespace errors.

gpu_execution_evidence: reports/j-7ded586a983c/raw/gpu_server/server.log identifies AMD gfx950 execution, records Triton compilation warnings and real prefill batches; probe-summary.json records four HTTP 200 results. Post-run rocm-smi reported 0% utilization and 0% allocated VRAM.
remaining_limitations: The tiny random Llama fixture validates transport and engine execution only, not model semantic accuracy or Qwen behavior.
The HTTP GPU probe did not deterministically pause at the exact delayed-final-prefill abort window; that race is reproduced by focused scheduler regression fixtures.
No multi-GPU, pipeline-parallel, data-parallel, distributed, or multi-node runtime validation was performed.
No native C++ or FlyDSL source changed, so no native rebuild was applicable.
